defense_in_depth_findings.title: Ledger adapter import is not hash-bound in the release bindings
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: scripts/research/f017_representative_s2_release_wrapper_v1.py imports f017_representative_expert_ledger_adapter_v1 (sha256 3655b90cff0adb882f9c52c54a89baf5414cf86efaa203101d5487eb36901ee4 at the reviewed head) for the ledger==175 preflight guard, but the adapter is not one of the twelve sha256-pinned release bindings, so wrapper-side binding validation does not cover its bytes.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: the adapter is read-only and fail-closed, internally pins its sole data source (f017-representative-m1f0-real-execution-result-v1.json, sha256 dc53b458fe9c189b4cfbfd83889e7997aa5decba799c421944ac93edb237f190, verified present and matching at the reviewed head), has no checkpoint, shard, or compute capability, and any adversary able to swap it on disk could equally swap the wrapper itself, which runtime self-pinning can never prevent; execution authority remains the reviewed committed bytes at the execution code head. Recommend adding the adapter to the bindings census in any future release version.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Committed synthetic rehearsal output hash is not byte-reproducible from committed bytes
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-representative-s2-synthetic-rehearsal-v1.json records synthetic input sha256 values and a fresh-process output sha256 (b01f0bf0...), but the synthetic input bytes and their generator are not committed, so the recorded output hash cannot be independently recomputed byte-for-byte.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: every load-bearing rehearsal property was independently re-established in this review with fresh synthetic inputs on the pinned runtime: 2-of-2 fresh-process bit-identical outputs through the committed executor CLI, all committed authorization and release mutations rejected (10/10 committed tests pass), exclusive-attempt race one winner one loser at process level, no-replace publication, and terminalizer reconciliation including interrupted and poisoned states. The rehearsal artifact is evidence, not execution authority.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: machine_local_paths enumeration omits the terminal.json path
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The release's machine_local_paths section lists state_root, output, manifest, receipt, approval, and go_token but not $HOME/.local/share/pulsarmlx/f017/representative-s2-release-1/attempt-state/terminal.json, which the wrapper and terminalizer treat as required.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: the terminal path is fixed in the pinned wrapper code (fixed_paths), required by output_banking.matching_complete_terminal_required and single_use.terminalizer_required, and enforced by the committed terminalizer; the omission is descriptive only and creates no caller-selectable path.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Python-level home parameter on fixed_paths/execute
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: wrapper.fixed_paths(home=...) and wrapper.execute(..., home=...) accept a home override reachable only via Python import, used by tests; the CLI surface exposes no path selection and resolves Path.home() plus repository-relative constants only.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: no CLI flag or environment variable reaches the parameter, the release prohibits caller-selected input paths at the operational surface, and invoking the wrapper through anything other than the committed CLI already exceeds the reviewed execution authority; verified by direct probe that the CLI rejects any --release path other than the fixed repository release file (RELEASE_PATH).

statement: Independent adversarial review of exact committed bytes at 35a607896eab09fe985e43a5aab6eca839a866d9 on feat/017-real-checkpoint-runner. Authority chain independently recomputed from git-show bytes: all 12 release bindings, all 8 construction-authorization bindings, and all transitive S1/FFN reuse lineage bindings (17 further artifacts including execution evidence, reuse reviews, upstream releases, approvals, approval reviews, resolvers, semantic graph) recompute exactly; release sha256 1b05c093..., authorization b85b255f..., arithmetic contract abbf1583... match the banked cycle-01 review request; execution code head 3c200b62 is an ancestor of the reviewed head with every load-bearing script byte-identical between the two and only an append-only contract/docs commit between them; no approval, no independent-review evidence, and no GO token exist in the committed tree, and real_event_authorized is false everywhere. Arithmetic adjudication: S2_f32[k]=binary32(binary64(S1_f32[k])+FFN_f64[k]) is fully executable and bit-deterministic as committed on the pinned CPython 3.14.6 Darwin-arm64 runtime; struct.iter_unpack('<f') performs the exact binary32-to-binary64 widening, one scalar binary64 addition per coordinate with left promoted S1 and right FFN, round-to-nearest ties-to-even, one final binary64-to-binary32 conversion via struct.pack with ties-to-even, subnormals preserved unflushed, overflow fail-closed (no saturation), serialization contiguous C-order little-endian over increasing coordinates 0..6143, and no FMA, reduction, BLAS, GPU, numpy, or parallel arithmetic exists in the pinned code. An independent exact-rational oracle implementing two-step round-to-nearest-even (exact sum to binary64, then binary32) matched the committed executor bit-for-bit on 12288 coordinates spanning random broad-range, tie, near-tie double-rounding, subnormal, cancellation, and near-overflow cases, plus 20000 targeted hardware-addition probes, all exact; fresh-process determinism 2-of-2 identical. The proof/reference-derived versus production serial-f32 distinction is correctly adjudicated: the surface is labeled CANONICAL_F017_PROOF_REFERENCE_DERIVED_S2_SURFACE_INTENTIONALLY_NOT_CLAIMED_EQUIVALENT_TO_PRODUCTION_SERIAL_F32 in the release, authorization, arithmetic contract, and output manifest; production equivalence is NOT_PROVEN_AND_NOT_CLAIMED, no equivalence assertion exists anywhere in the package, serial-f32 substitution is prohibited and validator-enforced, and the committed discriminator (1.0 + (2^-24+2^-52) yielding 0x3f800001 versus serial-f32 1.0) was independently confirmed, so no unproven equivalence is accepted. Operand reuse lineage: S1 (sha256 8309377e..., 6144 f32, 24576 bytes) and FFN (sha256 4d7aaeb5..., 6144 f64, 49152 bytes) bind exactly through their accepted reuse authorizations to completed single-use releases with COMPLETE terminals, consumed tokens, and no retry/resume/second attempt; the executor enforces exact private-manifest census and binding, regular non-symlink single-hard-link read-only owner-only files, O_NOFOLLOW descriptor-relative opens against directory-substitution-checked roots, and EXPECTED=BEFORE=CONSUMED=AFTER on the same file descriptor with fstat identity before and after arithmetic, so historical or alternate operand substitution fails closed; no fallback compute path (checkpoint, shard, attention, S1 materialization, FFN or routed-aggregate or expert recomputation) exists in the pinned code, and no environment-variable or caller-selected path override exists beyond the required thread pins. Release mechanics verified by running the committed validator (REPRESENTATIVE_S2_RELEASE_VALID), the committed 10-test suite (all pass), and 33 additional adversarial probes at the reviewed bytes: fixed pathlib home and repository path resolution with caller-selected release path rejected; approval, review, and GO token strictly separated with exact-field-and-order, required-constant, reviewer-identity/model, review-verdict-ACCEPT-with-empty-blocking-and-non-blocking-required, review-path-confinement, and reviewed-head committed-release-bytes enforcement all rejecting mutation; token requires 0o400 single-link exact-field binding through the approval sha256; exclusive attempt creation via atomic mkdir with one winner and one loser at process level; durable fsynced attempt-start before any arithmetic and durable fsynced s2-start counting exactly one construction regardless of outcome; failure after start consumes the release with no retry, resume, or second attempt (preflight and begin_attempt both reject prior state); race losers never own state and cannot poison the winner's terminal, and terminal writes are no-replace; output publication is descriptor-relative exclusive-temp, fsynced, no-replace hard-link with readback verification; the execution receipt, private manifest, and COMPLETE terminal are mutually bound by sha256 and the terminalizer reconciles NOT_STARTED, interrupted, published-without-terminal (no authority, requires adjudication), failure, and poisoned states correctly, refusing partial output authority; accounting is truthful (ledger 175 invariant, zero checkpoint reads, zero shard opens, zero S1 materializations, zero FFN compositions, exactly one future S2 construction) and the stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_S2_OUTPUT_ONLY is respected with no post-terminal action. No real S1 or FFN operand bytes were read, no S1 materialization, FFN composition, S2 construction, checkpoint access, shard open, approval, or GO token was performed or created during this review; all dynamic testing used synthetic operands in disposable temporary roots and a detached throwaway worktree left clean. Four defense-in-depth findings are recorded with concrete non-blocking dispositions; there are no blocking and no non-blocking-required findings. The committed package is sufficient for a later separate independent approval and exactly one future checkpoint-free S2 construction with no other execution authority. Verdict: ACCEPT.
